title: perf(losses): use separable kernels for float64 CPU MS-SSIM
body:
## What does this pull request do?

Large, multi-channel float64 `MS_SSIMLoss` calls spend most of their CPU time applying the same full 2-D Gaussian windows to five moment maps and the L1 difference. Use a horizontal and vertical grouped convolution when the computation is float64 on CPU, there is more than one channel, and the window is at least 17 taps wide.

The full-resolution, zero-padded formula, channel-major scale order, last-sigma luminance/L1 terms, reductions and output dtype are preserved. Float32, half precision, grayscale, smaller windows, other devices and legacy pickles without stored sigmas retain dense filtering. There is no new cache or public API.

An unrestricted float32 prototype was rejected: ordinary constant images at 0.5 and 0.5001 changed the loss by 0.000738 because of variance cancellation. Small-window and single-tap timings also regressed. The retained path addresses the measured float64 case, and all of those negative results remain in the [exploration record](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/blob/d2ffd4d6042f64a3f59e57bb2ffe8f624fa68bc9/.audit/kornia/ms-ssim-eager-exploration.json).

## Related issue or discussion

Implements a scoped form of the separable-Gaussian suggestion by @dodobyte in [#1850](https://github.com/kornia/kornia/issues/1850#issuecomment-1553684760). The idea predates this contribution. The [complete implementation-history audit](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/blob/b902fcf2fbc86ca0796ad7a986800c3742433728/.audit/kornia/ms-ssim-complete-history-summary.json) covers upstream PR heads, old fork branches, their intermediate commits and old class/file names; it found no prior separable MS-SSIM implementation.

## What did you check?

Exact final head: `21c8e92cb36341353d910d3922201805bcce4400`; base: `b1624c022ceb93373cb073a50bd1da2511108c5e`.

On CPU with PyTorch 2.5.1 and 2.15.0, each:
- 167 affected eager SSIM tests passed; 5 cases were deselected by the selection below.
- 100 public-API comparisons cover textured, near-identical and constant images; alpha 0, 0.025 and 1; two, three and four channels; batch broadcasting, strided inputs, 17/15-tap boundaries, grayscale, one-tap kernels, float32/float16/bfloat16 and an old pickle.
- All 55 fallback cases match the base bit for bit in the loss map and both image gradients. The active float64 cases differ by at most 2.044e-10 in the loss map and 4.487e-12 in gradients, within unmodified default Torch tolerances, which are stricter than BaseTester defaults.
- A new hardcoded loss-map pin comes from independent direct 2-D NumPy correlation; its generating snippet is beside the test. A multichannel finite-difference gradcheck covers the optimized path.
- Full pre-commit and typecheck passed on the current locked development toolchain.

```text
pixi run -e py312 uv run --no-sync pytest tests/losses/test_ssim.py --device=cpu --dtype=float32,float64 -k "not jit and not compile and not dynamo and not onnx" -q
pixi run -e py312 uv run --no-sync pre-commit run --all-files
pixi run -e py312 typecheck
```

[Final validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43964266105). [Public-API comparison and timing run](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43963058324). The measured production AST at `a4c31b02` is identical to the final head; the final validation verifies that equality and repeats the numerical checks.

Timings use the public `MS_SSIMLoss` call, verified source paths, `common.warm_up_cpu`, and `common.time_us` median/IQR, on one CPU thread with Python 3.12.12 on the same Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64 runner. Two base and two candidate rounds run in B/C/C/B order. Ratios below divide the median base timing by the median candidate timing; each entry is forward / forward+backward.

| Float64 workload, default 33-tap window | Torch 2.5.1 | Torch 2.15.0 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1 x 3 x 16 x 16 | 3.71x / 4.22x | 4.10x / 4.45x |
| 1 x 3 x 64 x 64 | 45.54x / 34.62x | 24.53x / 25.70x |
| 4 x 3 x 64 x 64 | 22.53x / 20.91x | 19.87x / 17.95x |

The 17-tap two-channel 16 x 16 case improves 1.48–1.62x across those modes/versions. Grayscale, small-window, one-tap and float32 fallback controls range from 0.978x to 1.011x, including the small slowdowns. These are CPU workload measurements; no accelerator speedup is claimed. [Machine-readable measurements](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/blob/df0a9e9fdf8506b2f07a2e2e18fae2542520182b/.audit/kornia/ms-ssim64-public-api-results.json).

**Draft validation limit:** the package/importer torch.compile and ONNX conformance selections required by TESTING.md remain unverified, as do TorchScript, CUDA and MPS. The completed eager CPU checks do not replace those gates; this contribution remains a draft pending them.

## Which part was done by a human, if any?

Afloat16 set the contribution scope and required new, non-duplicate changes with practical benefit. OpenAI Codex (GPT-6 Astra Pro) performed the technical investigation, implementation, and validation reported above.

Posted on behalf of @Afloat16 by OpenAI Codex (GPT-6 Astra Pro).
